stats.nodeMetrics.title: Node metrics
stats.nodeMetrics.description: The machine's own totals, not the sum of the workloads it is carrying.
stats.nodeMetrics.footer: Node {nodeId}. The window this page opened on ran from {from} to {to}; raw samples are kept for two days and hourly and daily buckets for a year.
stats.serviceMetrics.title: Metrics · {name}
stats.serviceMetrics.descPlaced: Pushed by the node holding this service, every fifteen seconds while it runs.
stats.serviceMetrics.descUnplaced: Nothing is running this service, so nothing is being measured right now. Anything already recorded is still here.
stats.serviceMetrics.emptyDesc: A node measures a workload while it is running and pushes the readings to the panel. This service has not been placed on one yet, so there is nothing to draw - start it and the first points arrive within a few seconds.
stats.serviceMetrics.footer: Raw samples are kept for two days and rolled into hourly and daily buckets after that, so a long window is drawn from averages. The window this page opened on ran from {from} to {to}.
stats.serviceLogs.title: Logs · {name}
stats.serviceLogs.descCron: One scheduled run, from the node that executed it.
stats.serviceLogs.descContainer: Everything {name} writes to stdout and stderr, tailed from the node holding it. The last {tailLines} lines arrive first.
stats.serviceLogs.emptyDesc: Logs are read from the container, so there has to be one. Start {name} and this page will follow its output from the first line - the panel does not keep a copy, so there is nothing here from before it was placed on a node.
stats.serviceLogs.footer: This is a tail, not an archive. The panel keeps no copy of container output, so what is on screen is what the node still holds - build logs are the exception and live on their deployment.
stats.dashboard.errorTitle: That range could not be read
stats.chart.empty: Nothing was measured in this window.
stats.summary.empty: Nothing has been measured in this window yet. A node pushes readings while a workload is running, so a service that has never started has nothing here.
stats.console.streamDropped: The stream dropped. It reopens by itself, asking the node for everything since the last line - so nothing written in between is lost.
stats.console.emptyPlaced: Nothing has been written yet. This is a live tail, so anything the container prints from now on appears here.
stats.console.emptyUnplaced: Nothing is running this service, so there is no output to tail.
stats.logNotice.dropped: --- {count} bytes of output were dropped: the container wrote faster than this could be read ---
stats.logNotice.ended: --- the source ended: the container exited, or the run finished ---
